B"H
# Phase 5 — Architecture Critique: Twenty-Four Corrections Before Code

> Chesed wants every frame; Gevurah asks what each vessel can truly hold;
> Tiferes joins them without false promises, as the Awtsmoos makes the many bold.

## Improvements over the first brainstorm
1. Do not build another renderer; reuse Animator.
2. Do not make every app render 3D; expose capability truth.
3. Put shared semantics in `shared/movie`, matching repo convention.
4. Keep the shared schema renderer-neutral.
5. Preserve millisecond timing because Animator already uses it.
6. Provide adapters for second-based NLEs.
7. Treat scenes and sequences as semantic blocks, not media clips only.
8. Carry cameras as first-class entities.
9. Carry particles/effects as first-class semantic entities.
10. Carry infographic primitives explicitly: chart, callout, arrow, label, meter.
11. Carry tutorial steps explicitly so AI can explain procedures.
12. Carry character roles and performances separately from visual shape data.
13. Carry 2D/3D dimensional intent per scene/entity.
14. Preserve unsupported source data in adapter metadata instead of silently discarding it.
15. Return adapter reports listing preserved, flattened, and unsupported features.
16. Make validation reject negative timing and timeline overflow.
17. Make IDs deterministic when AI omits them.
18. Make prompt/intent generation deterministic enough for tests.
19. Keep AI intent compiler separate from app adapters.
20. Add capability negotiation before choosing an app target.
21. Avoid current hot Animator/Mitzvah UI files until hashes stabilize.
22. Prove the architecture through a real 180-second project, not a toy fixture.
23. Validate cross-app projections of that same project.
24. Browser-test actual mobile layouts after source integration, not only Node imports.

## Failure map
- Schema too weak -> AI invents unrenderable fields. Counter: normalized factories + validator.
- Schema too narrow -> tutorials/infographics collapse into text. Counter: semantic entity kinds.
- Fake unification -> every app claims all features. Counter: capability manifest + projection report.
- Renderer coupling -> shared modules import Animator internals. Counter: adapters own app-specific imports.
- Concurrent overwrite -> lost work. Counter: new-file-first design and hash-guarded rewrites.
- Three-minute proof too repetitive -> false breadth. Counter: acceptance metrics for scene kinds, cameras, shapes, effects, people, and transitions.
